title: Bram and the Drop
premise: Ada Okafor, a disgraced intelligence analyst, receives a calendar invite from her dead handler, Bram Voss, summoning her to a meeting already underway. Pulled into an off-book extraction of Marek Dusek, a defector who may be the bait in someone else's trap, Ada must move him across the border before the checkpoint shifts change at dawn. As she unravels who killed Bram and why his ghost scheduled the meeting, she discovers the operation was designed to burn her for good. In the end, Ada chooses truth over loyalty: she exposes the mole inside her old agency, lets Dusek go free rather than trade him, and walks away from the service that discarded her — alive, unattributed, and finally her own.
about_author: Emrys Yarrow is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade writing briefings no one read before turning to fiction instead. Yarrow lives near a border town whose checkpoints inspired much of this novel's geography.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Three months after handler Bram Voss's funeral, Ada receives a calendar invite from his account for a meeting starting tomorrow at a café she's never used. She verifies he's dead — twice. The beat is cold dread sharpening into obsession: grief curdling into the first question she can't put down.

chapters.title: Café Meridian
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. She goes anyway. Instead of Bram, she finds Marek Dusek, a jittery defector clutching Bram's notebook, and two watchers she makes immediately. A quiet handoff becomes a running fight through the market district. The beat: adrenaline and betrayal — someone wanted her here, and it wasn't Bram's ghost alone.

chapters.title: What the Notebook Says
chapters.summary: POV: Ada, with an intercut of Bram's final day. The notebook contains fragments: a payment trail, a codename — LANTERN — and a note in Bram's hand: 'If you're reading this, I'm the drop.' Ada realizes Bram anticipated his own murder. The beat: vertigo; the case was built around her from the start.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Home
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. She works old contacts for safe passage and learns every door is watched — someone flagged her as hostile in all three agencies that fired her. Only Ilse Brandt, a retired forger who owes Bram, will help. The beat: isolation deepening into grim resolve; loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Defector's Story
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Ada and Dusek. Dusek confesses what he actually stole: not state secrets but proof that LANTERN sold the location of a prior extraction team, killing four. He doesn't know who LANTERN is — but knows the exchange point. The beat: reluctant trust forming between two people using each other.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. She maps the border crossing: shift change at 04:40 leaves a nine-minute gap, but the route requires a vehicle Ilse can only half-provide. Meanwhile she decodes a second layer in Bram's notes pointing to someone inside her former agency. The beat: ticking-clock pressure fusing with personal dread.

chapters.title: Lantern
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Following the money, she identifies LANTERN: Deputy Director Corin Hale, the man who once mentored her and signed her dismissals. He calls her personally, offering reinstatement if she delivers Dusek — and a quiet threat if she doesn't. The beat: love against duty inverted; the father figure revealed as the predator.

chapters.title: The Long Road North
chapters.summary: POV: Ada and Dusek. The drive to the border under false plates, pursued by a clean-up team Hale dispatched. An ambush at a fuel stop costs them the primary vehicle and nearly Dusek's life. Ada chooses to keep going off-plan. The beat: commitment — no exit left that isn't forward.

chapters.title: Nine Minutes
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. At 04:31 they hit the checkpoint zone on foot through drainage culverts. Hale waits inside the gap, having predicted her route from Bram's own playbook. Confrontation in the floodlit corridor between fences: Hale offers her Bram's job, Dusek's life for her silence. The beat: climax — Ada refuses, triggers the alarm herself, forcing exposure.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. In the chaos, Dusek crosses; Hale is arrested when Ada's dead-drop of the ledger reaches three journalists simultaneously. Weeks later, cleared but unmourned by the agencies, Ada visits Bram's grave and leaves the notebook. The beat: resolution — justice outside the law achieved, loyalty honored, and freedom chosen over belonging.
